[[Category:Probability]]
[[Category:Information theory]]
The '''Shannon entropy''' is the '''entropy''' of a probability distribution, measuring the uncertainty associated with a discrete [[random variable]]. 

It generalises the idea of information content to discrete probability distributions.

== Definition ==

Let $X$ be a discrete [[random variable]] with support $\mathcal{X}$, and $p_X(x)=\Pr(X=x)$ its probability mass function.

Then its '''Shannon entropy'''

$$
H(X)=-\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}}p_X(x)\log_b p_X(x).
$$

By convention, $0\log_b 0=0$.

The base $b$ determines the unit of the entropy:

<div class=center>
{| class="wikitable"
|-
! $b$
! Unit
|-
| $2$
| Bit
|-
| $e$
| Nat
|-
| $10$
| Hartley
|}
</div>

<blockquote>
One unknown binary digit represents $1 \mathrm{bit}$ of uncertainty, one unknown decimal digit represents $1 \mathrm{hartley}$ of uncertainty, one unknown digit in base $b$ represents $1 \mathrm{unit}$ of uncertainty when $b$ is chosen as the log base.
</blockquote>

== Interpretation ==

'''Shannon entropy''' is the '''expected surprise''':

$$
H(X)=\mathbb{E}\left[-\log_b p_X(X)\right].
$$

It measures the average amount of uncertainty about the outcome of $X$ before it is observed.

Higher entropy means greater uncertainty and less predictability. Lower entropy means greater predictability and more concentrated probability mass.

Contrary to the [[variance]] and [[standard deviation]] of a discrete probability distribution, '''entropy''' depends only on the probability distribution of $X$, but not on the numerical values taken by $X$. 

== Properties ==

=== $0\le H(X)\le \log_b|\mathcal{X}|$ ===

for a discrete random variable $X$ with support $\mathcal{X}$, where $|\mathcal{X}|$ is the number of possible outcomes. 

The upper bound is attained exactly when $X$ is '''uniformly distributed''' over $\mathcal{X}$.

== Two random variables ==

=== Joint entropy ===

For two discrete random variables $X,Y$ with support $\mathcal{X,Y}$, the '''joint entropy''' is

$$
H(X,Y)=-\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}}\sum_{y \in \mathcal{Y}}p_{X,Y}(x,y)\log_b p_{X,Y}(x,y),
$$

=== Conditional entropy ===

The '''conditional entropy'''

$$
H(Y\mid X)=H(X,Y)-H(X)
$$

measures the remaining uncertainty about $Y$ after $X$ is known. 

=== Mutual information ===

The '''mutual information'''

$$
I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)
$$

measures the reduction in uncertainty about $X$ obtained by observing $Y$.
